extracted.intended_audience: general readers and businesspeople interested in Andrew Carnegie's life, business practices, and advice
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted principles and practical guidance embedded in an autobiographical chapter describing Carnegie's business decisions, personal rules, and reflections on industry, policy, and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial independence through ownership/control
rubrics_metrics.description: A man must necessarily occupy a narrow field who is at the beck and call of others; even presidents of corporations are hardly their own master unless they hold control of the stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ownership or controlling interest to be independent in decision-making; recognize that boards and shareholders can hamper the ablest presidents. Carnegie states this as a reason for leaving salaried employment and working only when he had control of ventures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculative trading and retain focus on core business
rubrics_metrics.description: I have adhered to the rule never to purchase what I did not pay for, and never to sell what I did not own; do not buy or sell stock speculatively or allow Stock Exchange fluctuations to distract management judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers and professional men should avoid owning exchange-traded stock to keep their minds calm and free; speculation is described as a parasite that creates no value and disturbs long-term judgment. Carnegie gives his personal rule and rationale (the 'molehill/mountain' perception from market swings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and invest in technical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open to new processes and first-of-a-kind machinery (example: building the first coal-washing and coking works in America based on knowledge from England).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reliable innovation is identified (Lauder's coal-washing), advance capital to build works, secure contracts for inputs, and appoint a competent superintendent. Early adoption can clear costs quickly and confer first-mover advantages; Carnegie emphasizes the public benefit and firm pride in turning waste into productive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire and promote on demonstrated merit and self-reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Value individuals who depend on themselves and seize opportunity rather than those who rely on hereditary rank or introductions; examples include Morrison rising from mechanic to superintendent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for initiative, independence, and demonstrated competence when advancing employees; avoid privileging social rank or connections over proven ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation in public policy positions (avoid extremes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppose extremes—neither unreasonable protectionism nor unrestrained free trade; favor balanced, moderated tariff policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with political leaders pragmatically to shape policy (Carnegie describes negotiating reductions and working with leaders across party lines). The criterion is to favor reasonable, practical solutions over ideological purity; use evidence and coalition-building to influence legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use travel and cultural education to sharpen judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Exposure to European art, sculpture, and music enlarges appreciation and leads one to unconsciously reject what is false or pretentious; travel provides new standards by which to judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately seek out masterpieces and cultural experiences (museums, concerts, cathedrals) to elevate tastes and refine critical judgment that will inform business and personal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive, detailed preparation in negotiations and finance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare clear prospectuses, anticipate legal counsel changes, and be ready to propose precise textual amendments (Carnegie sent a line-by-line telegram of changes to bonds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work out detailed contractual language in advance; anticipate objections and show readiness to act quickly. Use facts (e.g., government charter) to counter criticisms and build banker confidence. Carnegie's anecdote with Junius Morgan illustrates the value of thorough, fast, and exact preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public relations and the press strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: A favorable mention from a respected financial editor can materially improve the market reception of securities; engage the press to highlight strengths and address objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify influential journalists or editors and give them the facts that meet public concerns (Carnegie used the Times' Sampson to emphasize the federal charter backing for the bridge bonds), thereby supporting pricing and market confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise prudence when accepting non-cash compensation or contingent payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts that take bonds and stocks in payment may succeed operationally but carry financial risk (Keokuk bridge succeeded technically but profits were lost due to a panic and bankrupt connecting railways).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accepting alternative forms of payment, assess counterparty risk and market conditions; be prepared for downstream financial unpredictability even if the undertaking itself is well executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain personal and professional courtesy when departing positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie's farewell letter to officers and employees expresses deep regret at parting, gratitude for kindness, and encouragement to support his successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resigning or changing roles, leave on respectful terms, thank colleagues sincerely, and request their support for successors to preserve goodwill and future relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set life goals including limits on accumulation and a plan for philanthropy
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie's memorandum: aim for a certain income, then stop accumulating wealth, settle in Oxford for education, engage in public matters, and spend surplus yearly for benevolent purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a deliberate plan for when to cease active wealth accumulation and how to deploy surplus for public benefit; outline practical next steps (education, cultural engagement, purchase of media to influence public discourse) rather than vague intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep organizational role aligned with comparative advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie shifted from hands-on operational roles in Pittsburgh to directing general company policy and negotiating major contracts from New York, while partners handled local operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign roles based on where individuals add most value: senior figures should concentrate on strategy, policy, and high-level negotiations, delegating day-to-day manufacturing management to capable partners.
